definition_zh: 温暖；暖和；热情；热心；（色彩）暖调
definition_en: the state of being warm, or the friendly feeling shown to others
core_image: 两只手握着一杯热茶，热气慢慢升上来
scene: 雪后的屋子里，炉火刚点起来，玻璃上蒙了一层白雾。 We stood by the stove and felt the warmth come back into our hands.
sceneCN: 这里 warmth 是「温暖」（第 1 个义项：暖和的状态）；句意为我们站在炉边，感到手渐渐回暖。握杯热茶时那股慢慢升起来的热，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 温暖；暖和；热情；热心；暖调

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -th 得到的形容词，义为「暖的；热情的」
warm 加 -ly 构成，义为「温暖地；热情地」
加 -less 构成，义为「无暖意的」

senses.title: The state of being warm
senses.definition: a moderate degree of heat, comfortable rather than hot
senses.definitionCN: 适中、令人舒适而不烫的热度
senses.example: We stood by the stove and felt the warmth come back into our hands.
senses.exampleCN: 我们站在炉边，感到手渐渐回暖。
senses.why: Warm is the adjective, and -th turns it into the noun for the state itself, as true turns to truth.
senses.whyCN: warm 是形容词，-th 把它变成表示状态本身的名词，正如 true 变 truth。

senses.title: Friendly feeling shown
senses.definition: kindness and friendliness in manner, which people feel as comfort
senses.definitionCN: 举止中的善意与亲切，让人感到舒适
senses.example: The warmth of the welcome surprised the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 主人的热情让来访者十分意外。
senses.why: Bodily heat is a comfort, and a friendly manner gives the same comfort, so the word carries over without effort.
senses.whyCN: 身上的暖是舒适，亲切的态度也给出同样的舒适，于是词义自然沿用。

senses.title: Heat in a place or an object
senses.definition: the heat stored in something, as felt by touch
senses.definitionCN: 物体存有的热，可凭触觉感到
senses.example: The warmth of the stone bench stayed after sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 石凳上的热在日落后仍未散。
senses.why: A stone keeps the heat it has taken, and the word for the state simply stays with the object.
senses.whyCN: 石头会留住它所吸收的热，表示这种状态的名词便留在了物体上。

senses.title: The warm quality of a colour
senses.definition: the effect of colours such as red and yellow, which seem to give off heat
senses.definitionCN: 红黄一类颜色给人的、仿佛散发热量的感觉
senses.example: The painter added warmth to the grey street with a few red roofs.
senses.exampleCN: 画家用几片红屋顶给灰冷的街道添了暖调。
senses.why: Reds and yellows recall fire and sun, so painters describe them with the same word for heat.
senses.whyCN: 红与黄让人想到火与太阳，画家于是用表示热的同一个词来描述它们。

senses.title: Heat in a voice or a sound
senses.definition: a quality in a voice that sounds kind, full and alive
senses.definitionCN: 声音中显得亲切、饱满而有生气的特质
senses.example: There was warmth in her voice that the letter could not carry.
senses.exampleCN: 她声音里的暖意是信里带不出来的。
senses.why: A kind voice gives the listener the same comfort as heat gives the skin, so the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 和善的声音给听者的舒适，正如热给皮肤的舒适，这个词便两处都用。

intro.en: Warmth is warm plus the old noun ending -th, which turns an adjective into a state.
intro.cn: warmth 是 warm 加古老的名词词尾 -th，把形容词变成状态名词。

items.en: The adjective had a root meaning warm in Old English, with a related noun for heat.
items.cn: 这个形容词的古英语形式本有「暖」的含义，并有表示热的相关名词。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic tongues all mean warm.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中的相关形式都表示「暖」。

items.en: The noun warmth settled in the Middle English period beside older forms now lost.
items.cn: 名词 warmth 在中古英语时期定型，与已废弃的更旧形式并存。

items.en: The -th ending is the same one in truth, length and depth.
items.cn: -th 词尾与 truth、length、depth 中的相同。

items.en: The sense of friendship and the sense of colour warmth both developed in modern usage.
items.cn: 友谊义与色彩暖调义都在现代用法中形成。

note.en: The first group holds the words of the same family, the second the other words for heat and kindness.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词，第二组收表示热与亲切的其他词。

examples.cn: 幸存者重建了家园。

dict_mnemonic.text: survive 是幸存，-or 表示人，survivor 就是「幸存者、生还者」。

root: 由 survive 加表示人的后缀 -or 构成，深层来自拉丁语 super（超过）与 vivere（活着）。

sensesIntro.en: Survivor means a person who lives through danger or hardship.
sensesIntro.cn: survivor 指闯过危险或艰难而活着的人。

core.en: The one who comes back from danger.
core.cn: 从危险中回来的人。

branches.en: The rescue team found the only survivor.
branches.cn: 救援队找到了唯一的幸存者。

branches.en: The survivors were taken to a safe place.
branches.cn: 幸存者被带到安全的地方。

branches.en: She is a survivor of a long illness.
branches.cn: 她是一场长期疾病的幸存者。

branches.en: An accident and an illness can both leave survivors.
branches.cn: 事故与疾病都会留下幸存者。

branches.en: He wrote a book as a survivor of the war.
branches.cn: 他作为战争幸存者写了一本书。

intro.en: Survivor relates to survive and survival, with the person suffix -or.
intro.cn: survivor 与 survive、survival 相关，带人物后缀 -or。

latinIntro.en: The Latin vivere, to live, is the deepest root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vivere（活着）是最深层的词根。

latinEntries.example: Super adds the sense of beyond.

definition_en: to make an idea or feeling understood, or to carry something to a place
core_image: 一辆小车沿着窄路，把箱子从这头稳稳送到那头
scene: 她没说一句重话，只用一个眼神就让满屋的人明白了意思。 Her silence conveyed more than any speech.
sceneCN: 这里 convey 指「传达」（第 1 个义项：把想法或信息传递给别人）；句意是她的沉默传达的意思胜过任何言语。

senses.title: To make understood
senses.definition: to make an idea or piece of information clear to other people
senses.definitionCN: 使想法或信息被别人清楚地理解
senses.example: Words cannot convey how grateful I am.
senses.exampleCN: 言语无法传达我有多么感激。
senses.why: A thought locked in one head is silent until something carries it out.
senses.whyCN: 锁在一个脑子里的想法是无声的，直到有东西把它运出去。

senses.title: To carry to a place
senses.definition: to take people or goods from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把人或货物从一处送到另一处
senses.example: The pipes convey water to the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这些管道把水送到村里。
senses.why: Before a word could mean to tell, it meant to carry.
senses.whyCN: 在表示告诉之前，这个词先表示搬运。

senses.title: To show a feeling
senses.definition: to let a feeling be seen or felt without stating it plainly
senses.definitionCN: 不必明说，就让某种情感被看见或被感到
senses.example: Her smile conveyed quiet confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的微笑传达出安静的自信。
senses.why: A face can carry a message further than a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 一张脸能把消息送得比一句话更远。

intro.en: Convey comes from Old French conveier, to escort, from Latin conviare, built from com-, together, and via, a way.
intro.cn: convey 来自古法语 conveier（护送），源于拉丁语 conviare，由 com-（一起）与 via（道路）构成。

items.en: Via meant a road or a way through.
items.cn: via 意为道路或通行的路线。

items.en: Conviare meant to travel together along a road.
items.cn: conviare 意为沿路一同行走。

items.en: Old French conveier meant to escort a person on the way.
items.cn: 古法语 conveier 意为在路上护送某人。

items.en: English convey first meant to carry or transport goods.
items.cn: 英语 convey 最初指搬运或运输货物。

items.en: The sense widened to carrying ideas and feelings.
items.cn: 词义扩大，开始指传递想法与情感。

items.en: Today it is used as often for meaning as for goods.
items.cn: 今天它用于含义的频率不亚于用于货物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin way base via-, and the meaning group names other verbs of carrying or telling.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的道路词基 via-，近义组列出其他表示运送或表达的说法。

entries.definition: a group of vehicles travelling together
a machine that carries things along
entries.definitionCN: 沿线路运送东西的机器

entries.definition: a person sent to speak for a country
to make information known to others
to carry goods from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 把货物从一处运到另一处

entries.definition: to show a thought or feeling in words
entries.definitionCN: 用言语表达想法或感情

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a cart on a road, then move to a message crossing a room and to a feeling shown on a face.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从路上的一辆车开始，再到一条消息穿过房间，最后到脸上的表情。

normal.en: Con- is together and vey is a way, so convey is to travel a road with something and hand it over.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，vey 是路，convey 就是带着东西走一段路，再交到别人手里。

normal.en: A truck conveys boxes; a sentence conveys a thought.
normal.cn: 卡车运送箱子，句子运送想法。

normal.en: The word hides via, the Latin road, in its last three letters.
normal.cn: 这个词最后三个字母里藏着拉丁语的道路 via。

normal.en: If the listener understands, the delivery has arrived.
normal.cn: 只要听的人懂了，这趟运送就算送到了。

normal.en: A quiet look can convey what shouting cannot.
normal.cn: 一个安静的眼神，能传达喊叫传达不了的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow road with one cart moving steadily.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄路上，一辆小车稳稳前行。

abstract.en: Picture a paper note passed hand to hand across a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条在房间里被一只手传到另一只手。

abstract.en: Picture a warm light carried from one window to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一点暖光从一扇窗被带到下一扇窗。

examples.en: He struggled to convey his excitement in English.
examples.cn: 他努力用英语表达自己的兴奋。

examples.en: The river conveys silt to the plain each spring.
examples.cn: 每年春天，这条河把泥沙运到平原。

examples.en: A short note can convey a great deal of warmth.
examples.cn: 一张短笺能传达许多暖意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 convey 记成 con（一起）加 vey（路）：陪着东西走一段路，就是运送，也就是把意思送到别人心里。

root: 源自拉丁语 via（道路），经 conviare（同行）与古法语 conveier（护送）进入英语，本指沿路运送，后引申为传达与表达。

sensesIntro.en: From goods carried along a road, to a thought carried into another mind, and at last to a feeling shown without words.
sensesIntro.cn: 从沿路运送的货物，到送进另一个头脑的想法，最后到不用言语表达的情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cart carrying a box along a narrow road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆小车沿着窄路运送一只箱子。

branches.en: A message crosses the gap between two minds.
branches.cn: 一条消息跨越两个头脑之间的空隙。

branches.en: A pipe or a cart moves real goods to a place.
branches.cn: 管道或车辆把真实货物送到某地。

branches.en: A face or a gesture carries a feeling without words.
branches.cn: 一张脸或一个手势不用言语就带出了情感。

branches.en: Both senses move something inward, one clear and one quiet.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把某种东西送进人心，一个清楚，一个安静。

branches.en: The physical trip came first, and the mental trip borrowed its shape.
branches.cn: 具体的运送先出现，心灵的传递借用了它的形状。

intro.en: Convey is built on Latin com-, together, plus via, a road, through the Old French verb conveier.
intro.cn: convey 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 via（道路）构成，经古法语动词 conveier 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The road base via- also shows in deviate, obvious and envoy.
latinIntro.cn: 道路词基 via- 也出现在 deviate、obvious 与 envoy 中。

items.meaning: the act or means of carrying
items.exampleCN: 公交车是公共交通工具。

items.meaning: a person sent on a way

items.example: Do not deviate from the plan.

items.meaning: right in the way, plain to see

definition_en: the measured amount of electric force between two points in a circuit
core_image: 两根导线之间的落差，像水从高处落向低处
scene: 维修工把表笔分别搭在插座的两个孔上，屏幕立刻跳出一个数字。 He checked the voltage before touching any wire in the old house.
sceneCN: 这里 voltage 是「电压」（第 1 个义项：两点之间的电势差）；句意为他在碰这栋老房子里任何电线之前先量了电压。表笔一搭、数字跳出，正是这个词所指的量。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -age 得到的单位名，义为「伏特」
加 -ic 构成，义为「伏打电流的」
复合形容词，义为「高压的；精力充沛的」

senses.title: The force between two points
senses.definition: the difference in electric potential between two points, which drives a current
senses.definitionCN: 两点之间的电势差，正是它推动电流
senses.example: He checked the voltage before touching any wire in the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 在碰这栋老房子的任何电线之前，他先量了电压。
senses.why: Volt is the unit; -age makes a noun of amount, so voltage is literally how many volts lie between two points.
senses.whyCN: volt 是单位，-age 把量变成名词，所以 voltage 字面上就是两点之间有多少伏。

senses.title: The value on a meter
senses.definition: the figure a meter shows for that force, as a measured value
senses.definitionCN: 仪表显示出的这个力的数值，作为测量结果
senses.example: The voltage on the screen rose slowly as the sun hit the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光照到面板上时，屏幕上的电压缓缓上升。
senses.why: Once a quantity can be read off a dial, the word refers to the figure itself rather than to the invisible push.
senses.whyCN: 量一旦能从表盘读出，这个词就指那个数字，而不是看不见的推力。

senses.title: A supply rated for a voltage
senses.definition: the level of electric force a device or a supply is built to use
senses.definitionCN: 电器或电源被设计使用的电力水平
senses.example: The lamp needs the right voltage or it will burn out.
senses.exampleCN: 这盏灯需要合适的电压，否则会烧坏。
senses.why: Manufacturers must state a level, so the word also names the condition a device expects.
senses.whyCN: 制造商必须标出水平，于是这个词也指设备所期待的条件。

senses.title: A difference to be stepped up or down
senses.definition: the level that transformers raise or lower between a power line and a home
senses.definitionCN: 变压器在电力线路与家庭之间升高或降低的水平
senses.example: A transformer cut the voltage before the current entered the street.
senses.exampleCN: 变压器在电流进入街道之前降低了电压。
senses.why: Because it is a difference between points, it can be changed up or down without any charge being created.
senses.whyCN: 因为它只是两点之间的差，所以可以随意升降，并不产生新的电荷。

senses.title: Lively force in a figurative sense
senses.titleCN: （比喻）高压般的劲头；激烈程度
senses.definition: in informal use, high energy or tension in a situation or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容场面或表演里的高能量与紧张感
senses.example: The band played with real voltage from the first bar.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队从第一小节起就带着十足的劲头。
senses.why: A high voltage is dangerous and hard to ignore, so the word has been borrowed for anything thrilling or tense.
senses.whyCN: 高电压危险又难以忽视，于是这个词被借来形容任何刺激或紧张的东西。

intro.en: Voltage is a plain English build on the unit volt: the unit plus the noun ending -age.
intro.cn: voltage 是在单位 volt 上做的普通英语构造：单位加名词后缀 -age。

items.en: The unit rests on the surname of Alessandro Volta, whose pile first gave a steady current.
items.cn: 单位建立在亚历山德罗·伏打的姓氏上，他的电堆首次提供稳定电流。

items.en: The unit name volt was agreed by electrical congresses in the eighteen sixties.
items.cn: 单位名 volt 由十九世纪六十年代的电学会议确定。

items.en: The ending came to English through the Old French noun ending that meant a state or a quantity.
items.cn: 这个后缀经由表示状态或数量的古法语名词词尾进入英语。

items.en: Voltage is recorded from the late nineteenth century, when ordinary households began to have wiring.
items.cn: voltage 自十九世纪后期有记录，当时普通家庭开始装电线。

items.en: Twentieth-century electronics added compound uses such as low voltage and voltage drop.
items.cn: 二十世纪的电子学又添出 low voltage、voltage drop 这类复合用法。

note.en: The first group gathers the words built on the unit, the second the other electrical quantities measured beside it.
note.cn: 第一组收以该单位为基础的词，第二组收与它并列测量的其他电学量。

entries.definition: The plural form of the noun.
The bare unit from which the noun is built.
An adjective meaning relating to current produced by chemical action.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「由化学作用产生电流的」。

entries.definition: The instrument used to read voltage.
The electric potential itself; the difference between two potentials is a voltage.
entries.definitionCN: 电势本身；两个电势之差就是电压。

entries.definition: The flow of charge, which a voltage drives.
entries.definitionCN: 电荷的流动，由电压推动。

entries.definition: The opposition to that flow.
The rate of energy delivered, voltage times current.
entries.definitionCN: 能量输送的速率，等于电压乘电流。

normalIntro.en: One unit, one suffix, and the electrical neighbours next door.
normalIntro.cn: 一个单位、一个后缀，再加上隔壁那几位电学邻居。

normal.en: Voltage is volt plus -age: a number of volts said as one quantity.
normal.cn: voltage 是 volt 加 -age：把若干伏特当一个量来说。

normal.en: Say a voltage of five volts, not a voltage of five.
normal.cn: 要说 a voltage of five volts，而不是 a voltage of five。

normal.en: Voltage drives, current flows, resistance opposes.
normal.cn: 电压推，电流流，电阻阻。

normal.en: A voltage drop is the fall between two points along a wire.
normal.cn: voltage drop 是沿导线两点之间的下降。

normal.en: High-voltage can describe a lively person as well as a line.
normal.cn: high-voltage 既能形容线路，也能形容精力充沛的人。

abstract.en: Picture water in a high tank, waiting for a tap to open.
abstract.cn: 想高塔里的水，等着水龙头打开。

abstract.en: See two ends of a wire at different heights on a climbing wall.
abstract.cn: 想一根导线的两端挂在攀岩墙的不同高度。

abstract.en: Feel the click of a switch making that difference do work.
abstract.cn: 感受开关一合，那个差开始干活。

examples.en: The voltage in this socket is too high for the small toy.
examples.cn: 这个插座的电压对这件小玩具来说太高了。

examples.en: Engineers lowered the voltage to protect the lamps.
examples.cn: 工程师降低电压以保护灯泡。

examples.en: A steady voltage keeps the machine running smoothly.
examples.cn: 稳定的电压让机器运转顺畅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「握太紧」——握住电线时手别太紧，先看清电压数字。

root: volt（伏特，来自意大利姓氏 Volta）+ 英语后缀 -age（量、状态）→ voltage；后缀经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One quantity grows four ways: an invisible difference between points, a figure on a dial, a level a device expects, and a level to be raised or lowered, before slipping into metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个量长出四重身份：两点间的无形之差、表盘上的数字、设备期待的额定水平、可以升高的等级，最后进入比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a difference in level between two ends of a wire.
core.cn: 核心意象：导线两端之间的高差。

branches.en: The physics branch: the push between two points.
branches.cn: 物理分支：两点之间的推力。

branches.en: The reading branch: what the screen shows.
branches.cn: 读数分支：屏幕上显示的数。

branches.en: The rating branch: the level a lamp needs.
branches.cn: 额定分支：灯泡所需的水平。

branches.en: The transformer branch: raised or lowered on the way to a street.
branches.cn: 变压器分支：进入街道前被升高或降低。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: a band playing with real voltage.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：乐队演奏带着十足的劲头。

intro.en: Volt- names a unit and -age turns it into a quantity; compounds then describe where that quantity goes.
intro.cn: volt- 是一个单位名，-age 把它变成量，复合词再说明这个量往哪里去。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root for electricity is involved; the base is an Italian surname, and only the suffix is a Latin-descended ending.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有表示电的拉丁词根，基底是意大利姓氏，只有后缀是拉丁来源的词尾。

items.example: The volt is the base of the name.
items.exampleCN: volt 是这个名称的基底。

items.meaning: a fall from one level to another

items.example: Volt- carries the person, not a meaning.
items.exampleCN: volt- 携带的是人名而非意义。

items.example: The voltaic cell is named for Volta.
items.exampleCN: voltaic cell（伏打电池）以伏打命名。

definition_en: to share or express sorrow for another person s trouble
core_image: 电话这头的人轻轻说「我懂」，声音放得很低
scene: 我同情你的处境。 I sympathize with your situation.
sceneCN: 这里 sympathize 是「同情」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我同情你的处境。

senses.title: To share someone s sorrow
senses.definition: to feel or express sorrow for another s trouble
senses.definitionCN: 为他人的困境感到或表达难过
senses.example: I sympathize with your situation.
senses.exampleCN: 我同情你的处境。
senses.why: The verb form of shared feeling names the act of standing with someone in pain.
senses.whyCN: 共同感受的动词形式，指在痛苦中与人站在一起的行为。

senses.title: To agree with a cause
senses.definition: to support an idea or movement
senses.definitionCN: 支持某种主张或运动
senses.example: Many readers sympathize with the writer s aim.
senses.exampleCN: 许多读者赞同作者的目标。
senses.why: Sharing a feeling grows into sharing a purpose, which gives the sense of support.
senses.whyCN: 共感会发展为共同的目标，于是产生支持之义。

senses.title: To explain kindly
senses.definition: to understand why someone acted as they did
senses.definitionCN: 理解某人为何如此行事
senses.example: She sympathized with his reasons.
senses.exampleCN: 她体谅他的理由。
senses.why: Understanding another s feeling includes understanding their motives, so the word also means to be understanding.
senses.whyCN: 理解他人的感受也包括理解其动机，因此这个词也表示体谅。

intro.en: Sympathize is the verb built on Greek sympatheia, shared feeling.
intro.cn: sympathize 是在希腊语 sympatheia（共同的感受）基础上构成的动词。

items.en: Sympatheia meant feeling together with another.
items.cn: sympatheia 意为与他人一同感受。

items.en: Pathos meant what is felt or suffered.
items.cn: pathos 意为所感或所受。

items.en: French sympathiser named sharing a feeling.
items.cn: 法语 sympathiser 指共享一种感受。

items.en: Sympathize entered English as to feel with.
items.cn: sympathize 进入英语时意为「一同感受」。

items.en: Sympathize extended to supporting a cause.
items.cn: sympathize 扩展到支持某项事业。

note.en: Sympathize is compared with look-alike words and with words for comforting.
note.cn: 把 sympathize 与形近词以及表示安慰的词作比较。

entries.definition: shared sorrow
caring about others
a sign for an idea
to comfort someone
to feel sorry for someone

normalIntro.en: Sympathize is the act of saying I feel this with you.
normalIntro.cn: sympathize 是说「我和你一起感受」的行为。

normal.en: I sympathize with your situation.
normal.cn: 我同情你的处境。

normal.en: Many readers sympathize with the writer s aim.
normal.cn: 许多读者赞同作者的目标。

normal.en: She sympathized with his reasons.
normal.cn: 她体谅他的理由。

normal.en: We sympathize with the families affected.
normal.cn: 我们同情受影响的家庭。

normal.en: He found it hard to sympathize with the decision.
normal.cn: 他很难对这个决定表示同情。

abstract.en: To sympathize is to make room for another s pain.
abstract.cn: 同情就是为他人的痛苦腾出空间。

abstract.en: Sympathy spoken aloud becomes sympathy shared.
abstract.cn: 说出口的同情才成为共享的同情。

abstract.en: We sympathize most easily with what we fear ourselves.
abstract.cn: 我们最容易同情自己所惧怕的处境。

examples.en: I sympathize with your situation.
examples.cn: 我同情你的处境。

examples.en: We sympathize with the families affected.
examples.cn: 我们同情受影响的家庭。

examples.en: She sympathized with his reasons.
examples.cn: 她体谅他的理由。

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · sym-（共同）+ path（感受）+ -ize（动词）
dict_mnemonic.text: sym- 表示共同，path 表示感受，-ize 使其成为动词；sympathize 即「共同感受」，也就是同情与赞同。

root: 来自希腊语 sympatheia（共同的感受），动词形式经法语 sympathiser 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Sympathize means to share sorrow, to support a cause, or to understand someone s reasons.
sensesIntro.cn: sympathize 表示分担悲伤、支持某项事业，或体谅他人的理由。

core.en: Standing beside someone and feeling with them.
core.cn: 站在他人身旁共同感受。

branches.en: I sympathize with your situation.
branches.cn: 我同情你的处境。

branches.en: We sympathize with the families affected.
branches.cn: 我们同情受影响的家庭。

branches.en: Many readers sympathize with the writer s aim.
branches.cn: 许多读者赞同作者的目标。

branches.en: She sympathized with his reasons.
branches.cn: 她体谅他的理由。

branches.en: He found it hard to sympathize with the decision.
branches.cn: 他很难对这个决定表示同情。

intro.en: Sympathize forms sympathizes, sympathized, sympathizing and sympathizer.
intro.cn: sympathize 可构成 sympathizes、sympathized、sympathizing 与 sympathizer。

latinIntro.en: Sympathize is Greek; the Latin equivalent is compati, to suffer with.
latinIntro.cn: sympathize 源自希腊语；拉丁语对应说法是 compati，意为一同承受。

items.exampleCN: 他写了一封表示同情的信。

latinEntries.example: Latin compati means to suffer with.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 compati 意为一同承受。

definition_en: a person whose job is to make and repair wooden objects and structures
core_image: 一个人弓着背，把木头一点点刨成想要的形状
scene: 木匠把一块松木刨成了桌面。 The carpenter planed a piece of pine into a tabletop.
sceneCN: 这里 carpenter 是「木匠」（第 1 个义项：制作和修理木器的人）；句意是木匠把一块松木刨成了桌面。

derivatives.zh: carpenter 加 -y 构成，义为「木工手艺、木作」
语义关联词，义为「细木工」，专做接合精细木件
语义关联词，义为「木工」，泛指以木材为材料的人

senses.title: A person who works with wood
senses.definition: a person whose job is to cut, shape, and join wood
senses.definitionCN: 以切割、成型和拼接木材为职业的人
senses.example: The carpenter repaired the broken chair.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠修好了那把坏椅子。
senses.why: Latin carpentum meant a wagon, and its maker, carpentarius, gave the word for a woodworker.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 carpentum 指马车，造车者 carpentarius 后来就成了「木匠」一词。

senses.title: A worker on the wooden parts of a building
senses.definition: a worker who builds the wooden frame, doors, and fittings of a house
senses.definitionCN: 负责房屋木构架、门和木制配件的人
senses.example: Carpenters raised the roof frame in one day.
senses.exampleCN: 木工们一天之内就立起了屋顶梁架。
senses.why: The same craft divides into furniture making and building work, so the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 同一门手艺分成做家具和做建筑两路，所以这个词两者都涵盖。

intro.en: Carpenter began as the name for a wagon maker, then settled on the worker in wood.
intro.cn: carpenter 最初指「造车的人」，后来固定指与木头打交道的工匠。

items.en: carpentum named a two-wheeled covered wagon, probably from a Celtic source.
items.cn: carpentum 指带篷的双轮车，可能源自凯尔特语。

items.en: carpentarius meant a wagon maker or a worker in wood.
items.cn: carpentarius 意为「造车者」或「木工」。

items.en: charpentier named the craftsman who built wooden frames and vehicles.
items.cn: 古法语 charpentier 指搭建木架、制造车辆的工匠。

items.en: English borrowed it as carpenter for anyone skilled in working wood.
items.cn: 英语借入为 carpenter，泛指擅长木作的人。

items.en: Today carpenter covers furniture makers, house framers, and repair workers alike.
items.cn: 今天 carpenter 同时涵盖做家具、搭屋架和修修补补的木工。

note.en: Carpenter has a craft noun in carpentry, and it sits beside other woodworking trades.
note.cn: carpenter 有对应的手艺名词 carpentry，同时和别的木工工种相邻。

entries.definition: the craft of working with wood
entries.definitionCN: 木工手艺，由 carpenter 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: a covered two-wheeled wagon in ancient Rome
entries.definitionCN: 古罗马的带篷双轮车，是 carpenter 的拉丁语源头。

entries.definition: a woodworker who makes joints and fitted furniture
entries.definitionCN: 细木工，专做榫接和嵌入式家具。

entries.definition: a person who makes things from wood
entries.definitionCN: 以木材制作物品的人，是更宽泛的说法。

entries.definition: a person or company that constructs buildings
entries.definitionCN: 建造房屋的人或公司，与建筑木工有工作交叉。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with car because the first carpenters built wagons.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词以 car 开头，因为最早的木匠就是造车的人。

normal.en: carpenter starts like car, and its Latin root carpentum meant a wagon.
normal.cn: carpenter 的开头像 car，其拉丁词根 carpentum 就指马车。

normal.en: carpentarius, the wagon maker, became the general word for a woodworker.
normal.cn: 造车者 carpentarius 后来成了泛指木工的词。

normal.en: carpentry is the craft, carpenter is the person.
normal.cn: carpentry 是手艺，carpenter 是人。

normal.en: carpenter's tools and carpenter's workshop are natural possessive phrases.
normal.cn: 木匠的工具、木匠的作坊，用所有格最自然。

normal.en: The plural carpenters adds only an s.
normal.cn: 复数 carpenters 只加一个 s。

abstract.en: Picture a plane sliding along a board and a curl of wood falling away.
abstract.cn: 想象刨子沿木板推过，卷起一条木花。

abstract.en: Picture a roof frame rising like a skeleton against the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象屋顶梁架像骨架一样在天空下立起。

abstract.en: Picture a hand testing a joint to see if it fits without a nail.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手试着接缝，看能不能不用钉子就严丝合缝。

examples.en: The carpenter planed a piece of pine into a tabletop.
examples.cn: 木匠把一块松木刨成了桌面。

examples.en: The carpenter repaired the broken chair.
examples.cn: 木匠修好了那把坏椅子。

examples.en: Carpenters raised the roof frame in one day.
examples.cn: 木工们一天之内就立起了屋顶梁架。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡盆特」——木头卡在盆边，特制的木匠来修。

root: 拉丁语 carpentum（车）→ carpentarius（造车者）→ 古法语 charpentier → 英语 carpenter。

sensesIntro.en: One craftsman, two workplaces: the furniture bench and the house frame.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个工匠，两个工作场所：做家具的工作台和房屋的梁架。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands guiding a tool along wood until the shape appears.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手引导工具沿木头推进，直到形状显现。

branches.en: The furniture sense: making and repairing wooden objects.
branches.cn: 家具义：制作和修理木制物件。

branches.en: The building sense: raising frames, doors, and fittings.
branches.cn: 建筑义：搭梁架、装门和木配件。

branches.en: Both senses share the same material and the same hand tools.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同样的材料和同样的手工工具。

branches.en: carpentry names the craft that a carpenter practises.
branches.cn: carpentry 指木匠所从事的手艺。

branches.en: On a building site the carpenter works beside bricklayers and roofers.
branches.cn: 在工地上，木工与砌砖工、屋面工并肩作业。

intro.en: Carpenter is an agent noun from Latin carpentarius, a wagon maker.
intro.cn: carpenter 是来自拉丁语 carpentarius（造车者）的施事名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin carpentum, a wagon, and carpentarius, its maker, are the root pair.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carpentum（车）与 carpentarius（造车者）构成词根对。

items.example: The carpenter measured the door twice.
Three carpenters worked on the frame.
He learned carpentry from his uncle.
Carpentum is the oldest form in the family.
items.exampleCN: carpentum 是这个词族里最古老的形式。
carpentarius 在法语中变成 charpentier。

items.example: The joiner fitted the cupboard doors.

items.meaning: a person who works with wood
items.exampleCN: 这位木工出售手工木碗。

items.meaning: a tool with a sharp edge for cutting wood
items.example: He cut the joint with a chisel.

definition_en: a long public argument about something that many people disagree on
core_image: 报纸上两封对开的来信，字句彼此顶撞
scene: 一份报告公布后，评论区吵了好几周。 The report caused a long controversy.
sceneCN: 这里 controversy 指「争议」（第 1 个义项：许多人之间持续很久的公开争论）；句意是这份报告引发了长时间的争议。

senses.title: A public quarrel
senses.definition: a long public argument among many people
senses.definitionCN: 许多人之间持续很久的公开争论
senses.example: The new road caused years of controversy.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新路引起了多年的争议。
senses.why: A crowd that cannot agree keeps the noise going.
senses.whyCN: 一群人若不能达成一致，声音就不会停。

senses.title: A dispute in words
senses.definition: a battle fought with statements rather than force
senses.definitionCN: 用言论而不是武力进行的交锋
senses.example: The two journals carried on a bitter controversy.
senses.exampleCN: 两家期刊打了一场激烈的论战。
senses.why: Ink can be as loud as a shout in a square.
senses.whyCN: 纸上的墨，也能像广场上的喊声一样响。

senses.title: A doubtful matter
senses.definition: a particular matter about which people hold opposite views
senses.definitionCN: 人们持相反看法的某一具体事件
senses.example: The choice of judge became a controversy of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 法官的人选本身成了一件有争议的事。
senses.why: Even the referee can become the match.
senses.whyCN: 连裁判也能变成比赛本身。

intro.en: Controversy comes from Latin controversia, a dispute, from controversus, turned against, built on contra-, against, and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: controversy 来自拉丁语 controversia（争执），源于 controversus（转向对立），由 contra-（反对）与 vertere（转）构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn one's body or a thing.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动身体或某物。

items.en: Controversus meant turned face to face in opposition.
items.cn: controversus 意为面对面转成对立。

items.en: Controversia named the dispute that such turning produced.
items.cn: controversia 指这种转向所产生的争执。

items.en: French controverse was used for learned debate.
items.cn: 法语 controverse 用于学术辩论。

items.en: English controversy named long public argument.
items.cn: 英语 controversy 指长期的公开争论。

items.en: It now covers disputes in law, science and daily life.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖法律、科学与日常生活中的争议。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin turning base vers-, and the meaning group names other words for open disagreement.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的转动词基 vers-，近义组列出其他表示公开分歧的词。

entries.definition: likely to cause public argument
to argue against a claim
in a way that stirs argument
a serious argument about something
a formal discussion of opposing views
a state of holding different opinions

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a crowd that cannot agree, then move to a war of ink and to a single doubtful matter.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从无法达成一致的人群开始，再到纸墨之战，最后到单独一件存疑之事。

normal.en: Contra- is against and vers is turn, so a controversy is sides turned against each other.
normal.cn: contra- 是相对，vers 是转，controversy 就是两方转过身来对着彼此。

normal.en: Old books fought their wars with ink.
normal.cn: 古书用墨打它们的仗。

normal.en: A controversy lasts because no side will sit down.
normal.cn: 争议之所以持久，是因为没有一方肯坐下。

normal.en: Even the choice of judge can become the fight.
normal.cn: 连选谁当裁判都能变成那场争斗。

normal.en: Two views, one public room, no exit.
normal.cn: 两种看法，一间公共的屋子，没有出口。

abstract.en: Picture two letters printed side by side, facing each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两封并排印出的信，彼此面对。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where each side holds a book.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，两方各抱一本书。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd splitting around one small table.
abstract.cn: 想象人群围绕一张小桌分成两边。

examples.en: The building plan caused great controversy.
examples.cn: 这项建筑计划引起了很大争议。

examples.en: He stayed at the centre of the controversy.
examples.cn: 他一直处在争议的中心。

examples.en: The controversy over the results lasted for months.
examples.cn: 关于结果的争议持续了好几个月。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 controversy 记成 contro（相对）加 vers（转）加 y：两方转过来对着彼此说，就是争论。

root: 源自拉丁语 controversia（争执），来自 controversus（转向对立），由 contra-（反对）与 vertere（转）构成，指长期公开的争论。

sensesIntro.en: From a crowd that cannot agree, to a war fought with ink, and at last to one matter that stays doubtful.
sensesIntro.cn: 从无法达成一致的人群，到用墨进行的战争，最后到一件始终存疑的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two letters printed side by side, facing each other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两封并排印出的信，彼此面对。

branches.en: A public argument is the everyday shape of the word.
branches.cn: 公开争吵是这个词最日常的形状。

branches.en: A war of printed words is its older shape.
branches.cn: 印刷文字之战是它更古老的形状。

branches.en: One doubtful matter can carry the whole name.
branches.cn: 一件存疑之事就能扛起整个名号。

branches.en: A crowd and a press can keep one argument alive.
branches.cn: 人群与报刊能让同一场争论活下去。

branches.en: Ink and doubt both keep a question from closing.
branches.cn: 墨与疑问都不让一个问题合上。

intro.en: Controversy is built on Latin contra-, against, plus vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: controversy 由拉丁语 contra-（反对）与 vertere（转）构成。

latinIntro.en: The turning base vers- also appears in convert, reverse and versatile.
latinIntro.cn: 转动词基 vers- 也出现在 convert、reverse 与 versatile 中。

items.meaning: a turning of sides against each other

items.example: He tried to controvert the claim.

items.meaning: in a way that stirs dispute
items.exampleCN: 这条规定的执行引发争议。

items.meaning: able to turn to many uses

definition_en: a person whose job is to cut and style people's hair
core_image: 镜前拿着剪刀的理发师
scene: 理发师给她剪了一个短发。 The hairdresser cut her hair short.
sceneCN: 这里 hairdresser 是「理发师」（第 1 个义项）；句意：理发师给她剪了一个短发。

senses.title: Cutter of hair
senses.definition: a person who cuts people's hair as a job
senses.definitionCN: 以替人剪发为职业的人
senses.example: The hairdresser cut her hair short.
senses.exampleCN: 理发师给她剪了一个短发。
senses.why: Cutting hair is the basic job sense.
senses.whyCN: 剪发，是这一职业最基本的义项。

senses.title: Shaper of styles
senses.definition: a person who also washes, colours, and styles hair
senses.definitionCN: 兼做洗、染与造型的人
senses.example: The hairdresser styled her hair for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 美发师为她的婚礼做了头发。
senses.why: The job widened from cutting to styling.
senses.whyCN: 这一职业从剪发扩展到造型。

intro.en: Hairdresser joins hair, from Old English, with dresser, from Old French dresser, to arrange.
intro.cn: hairdresser 由古英语的 hair 与古法语 dresser（整理）构成的 dresser 组合而成。

items.en: Hær meant hair.
items.cn: hær 意为头发。

items.en: Dresser meant to arrange or prepare.
items.cn: dresser 意为整理或准备。

items.en: A dresser was one who prepared or arranged.
items.cn: dresser 指整理或布置的人。

items.en: Hairdresser named one who arranges hair.
items.cn: hairdresser 指整理头发的人。

items.en: The trade grew to include washing and colouring.
items.cn: 这一行业扩展到洗发与染发。

note.en: Hairdresser is compared with look-alike words and words for people who care for hair.
note.cn: 把 hairdresser 与形近词以及表示美发从业者的词作比较。

entries.definition: the work of cutting and styling hair
a style of hair
a machine that dries hair
a person who cuts men's hair
a person who styles hair or clothes
a hairdresser, in formal use

normalIntro.en: A hairdresser is a person who dresses hair, first by cutting it and then by styling it.
normalIntro.cn: hairdresser 是「整理头发的人」，先剪，再造型。

normal.en: The hairdresser cut her hair short.
normal.cn: 理发师给她剪了一个短发。

normal.en: The hairdresser styled her hair for the wedding.
normal.cn: 美发师为她的婚礼做了头发。

normal.en: I have an appointment with the hairdresser.
normal.cn: 我和理发师约好了。

normal.en: The local hairdresser is very popular.
normal.cn: 本地这家理发店很受欢迎。

normal.en: She trained as a hairdresser for two years.
normal.cn: 她学了两年的美发。

abstract.en: Hair is cut once, but style is chosen many times.
abstract.cn: 头发只剪一次，风格却要反复选择。

abstract.en: A good hairdresser listens before cutting.
abstract.cn: 好的理发师，先听再剪。

abstract.en: Small changes at the head change the whole face.
abstract.cn: 头顶的小改变，改变整张脸。

examples.en: The hairdresser cut her hair short.
examples.cn: 理发师给她剪了一个短发。

examples.en: The hairdresser styled her hair for the wedding.
examples.cn: 美发师为她的婚礼做了头发。

examples.en: I have an appointment with the hairdresser.
examples.cn: 我和理发师约好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: hairdresser 由 hair（头发）加 dresser（整理者）构成，指「理发师、美发师」；go to the hairdresser 是去理发。

root: 由 hair（头发，古英语 hær）与 dresser（整理者，源自法语 dresser）组合而成；整理头发的人，就是理发师与美发师。

sensesIntro.en: Hairdresser means a person who cuts hair, or one who also styles and colours it.
sensesIntro.cn: hairdresser 指为人剪发的人，也指兼做造型与染发的人。

core.en: A person who arranges hair.
core.cn: 整理头发的人。

branches.en: Scissors move around a head.
branches.cn: 剪刀在头顶移动。

branches.en: A brush and dryer shape a style.
branches.cn: 梳子与吹风机做出造型。

branches.en: A mirror faces the chair.
branches.cn: 镜子正对椅子。

branches.en: Colour is mixed in a small bowl.
branches.cn: 染膏在小碗里调匀。

branches.en: The cutter and the stylist are one pair of hands.
branches.cn: 剪发与造型，是同一双手。

intro.en: Hairdresser forms plurals, an activity noun, and a shop noun.
intro.cn: hairdresser 构成复数、表示行业的名称，以及表示店铺的名称。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; hair is Germanic and dresser is French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根；hair 属日耳曼语，dresser 来自法语。

items.exampleCN: 这里有两名理发师工作。
美发是一门有技术的手艺。

items.meaning: the act or style of cutting hair

definition_zh: 图书馆员；图书馆管理员；图书馆馆长
definition_en: a person who works in or is in charge of a library, looking after books and helping readers
core_image: 书架间的过道上，一个人推着装满书的小车，把归还的书放回原位
scene: 闭馆前半小时，借书台前排起短队，穿灰毛衣的工作人员把每本书的磁条扫过感应器。 The librarian stamped the due date on the last book.
sceneCN: 这里是「图书馆员」（第 1 个义项：在图书馆工作的人）；句意为那位馆员在最后一本书上盖了到期日。图中可辨识物件：借书台、磁条感应器、装满书的小车。

pos.zh: 图书馆员；图书馆管理员；图书馆馆长

derivatives.zh: librarian 的词根名词，义为「图书馆；藏书」
由 librarian 加 -ship 构成，义为「图书馆工作；图书馆学」

senses.title: A person who works in a library
senses.definition: someone whose job is to work in a library, arranging books and helping people who come to read or borrow
senses.definitionCN: 在图书馆工作、整理书籍并帮助前来阅读或借书的人
senses.example: The librarian stamped the due date on the last book.
senses.exampleCN: 那位馆员在最后一本书上盖了到期日。
senses.why: Latin librarius meant of books and also a bookseller; adding -an makes a person connected with books, so the librarian is the one whose work is tied to the collection.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 librarius 意为与书有关的，也指书商；加上 -an 就得到「与书有关的人」，所以馆员就是工作与藏书绑在一起的人。

senses.title: The person in charge of a library
senses.definition: the head of a library, responsible for its budget, staff and collection
senses.definitionCN: 图书馆的负责人，掌管经费、人员与藏书
senses.example: As chief librarian, she decides which journals the college buys.
senses.exampleCN: 作为馆长，她决定学院购买哪些期刊。
senses.why: The title does not split between workers and the head: responsibility for the collection is still bookkeeping, so the same word covers the person in charge.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓并不在普通职员与负责人之间切开：对藏书的负责仍然是一种管书的事，所以同一个词也覆盖负责人。

senses.title: A specialist trained in organizing information
senses.definition: a trained professional who organizes, catalogues and searches information for users
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、为用户整理、编目与检索信息的专业人员
senses.example: A law librarian can find a case in minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 法律图书馆的信息馆员几分钟就能找到一个判例。
senses.why: As collections moved from paper to databases, the same title widened to cover the skills of cataloguing and searching, not only the handling of books.
senses.whyCN: 当藏书从纸张转向数据库，同一个称谓扩展到编目与检索的本领，不再只管搬书。

intro.en: Librarian grows out of the Latin word for book, through the Latin names for a bookseller and a place of books, and is completed by an English suffix for a person.
intro.cn: librarian 从拉丁语中表示「书」的词长出来，途经拉丁语里「书商」与「藏书之处」两个名字，最后由一个英语中指人的后缀收尾。

items.en: Liber first meant the inner bark of a tree, and because people wrote on that bark it came to mean a book.
items.cn: liber 最初指树的内皮，因为人们在这层皮上写字，它后来就指书。

items.en: Librarius meant belonging to books, and as a noun it named a bookseller or a copyist.
items.cn: librarius 意为与书有关的，作名词时指书商或抄写员。

items.en: Librarium was a place for books, the ancestor of the English word for a library.
items.cn: librarium 是存放书的地方，是英语中「图书馆」一词的祖先。

items.en: Library enters English through Old French librairie, at first naming a place or a collection of books.
items.cn: library 经古法语 librairie 进入英语，最初指藏书的地方或一批藏书。

items.en: Librarian is formed inside English by adding -an to library, and is recorded from the early eighteenth century.
items.cn: librarian 是在英语内部给 library 加 -an 造出来的，最早记录见于十八世纪初。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin book root and its English offspring; the near-meaning group gathers people who care for collections.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「书」的词根及其英语后代展开；近义组收照管藏书的人。

entries.definition: A place or a collection of books kept for reading and borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 供阅读与借阅的藏书地点或藏书。

entries.definition: The work or study of running a library.
entries.definitionCN: 经营图书馆的工作或学问。

entries.definition: The words of an opera, literally a little book, from the same Latin root through Italian.
entries.definitionCN: 歌剧的歌词本，字面是「小书」，经意大利语来自同一拉丁词根。

entries.definition: A published false statement, from a Latin little book, now far from its book sense.
entries.definitionCN: 公开发表的虚假陈述，来自拉丁语「小书」，如今已远离书的本义。

entries.definition: A person who looks after a collection.
entries.definitionCN: 照管一批藏品的人；馆长。

entries.definition: A person who keeps and organizes records.
A person who sells books.
A person who lists and describes items in a collection.
entries.definitionCN: 为藏品编目并加以描述的人。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for book plus an English ending for a person gives this job its name, and the family keeps the book at its centre.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「书」加一个英语中指人的词尾，给了这份职业名字，整族词始终把书放在中心。

normal.en: Liber is Latin for book, so library and librarian share one root.
normal.cn: liber 是拉丁语的「书」，所以 library 与 librarian 共用一个词根。

normal.en: The suffix -an marks a person connected with a place or a subject, as in librarian and historian.
normal.cn: 后缀 -an 标记与某个地方或学科有关的人，如 librarian 与 historian。

normal.en: Librarianship adds -ship, the ending for a job, a skill or an office.
normal.cn: librarianship 加的是 -ship，这个后缀表示职位、技能或职务。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: li-BRAR-i-an.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二个音节：li-BRAR-i-an。

normal.en: One title covers both the head of the library and the person at the desk.
normal.cn: 一个称谓同时覆盖馆长和坐在借书台前的人。

abstract.en: A word for a keeper of books reminds us that knowledge needs shelves as much as minds.
abstract.cn: 一个「看管书的人」的词提醒人：知识既需要头脑，也同样需要书架。

abstract.en: The same root gives library and libretto, a small book that holds the words of an opera.
abstract.cn: 同一词根给出 library 与 libretto，后者是装着歌剧歌词的小书。

abstract.en: A librarian is a bridge between a stored collection and a person who needs one page of it.
abstract.cn: 馆员是藏书与那个只需要其中一页的人之间的一座桥。

examples.en: The librarian stamped the due date on the last book.
examples.cn: 那位馆员在最后一本书上盖了到期日。

examples.en: As chief librarian, she decides which journals the college buys.
examples.cn: 作为馆长，她决定学院购买哪些期刊。

examples.en: A law librarian can find a case in minutes.
examples.cn: 法律图书馆的信息馆员几分钟就能找到一个判例。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来不来借」——来图书馆借书，找的就是 librarian。

root: 拉丁语 liber（书；树的内皮）→ librarius（与书有关的；书商）→ librarium（藏书之处）→ 英语 library，再加表「人」的 -an 成为 librarian。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person tied to a collection of books; the senses divide into the desk worker, the head of the library, and the trained information specialist.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是与一批藏书绑在一起的人；义项分为借书台前的职员、图书馆负责人，以及受过训练的信息专业人员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cart of returned books moving between shelves at closing time.
core.cn: 核心意象：闭馆时分，一辆装归还书的小车在书架间穿行。

branches.en: a cart of returned books moving between shelves
branches.cn: 一辆装归还书的小车在书架间移动

branches.en: a reader asking where a title is kept
branches.cn: 一位读者询问某本书放在哪里

branches.en: a head librarian signing a purchase order
branches.cn: 馆长签下一份采购单

branches.en: a search screen open beside a stack of journals
branches.cn: 一摞期刊旁开着的检索界面

branches.en: one title covering desk work, management and searching
branches.cn: 一个称谓同时覆盖借书台、管理与检索

intro.en: The Latin book root passes through the bookseller and the place of books, then English adds two suffixes that make a person and a profession.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「书」词根经过「书商」与「藏书之处」，再由英语加上两个后缀，造出「人」与「职业」。

latinIntro.en: Liber, librarius and librarium are recorded Latin words, and the English family grows directly from them.
latinIntro.cn: liber、librarius 与 librarium 都是有记录的拉丁词，英语这一族直接从它们长出来。

a place or thing connected with
a person who works with books

definition_en: to send out a programme by radio or television
core_image: 电台发射塔上亮着的红灯
scene: 收音机里传出熟悉的播音声。 The station will broadcast the match at eight.
sceneCN: 这里 broadcast 是「播送」（第 2 个义项：用电台或电视发送节目）；句意是电台将在八点播送这场比赛。

derivatives.zh: 宽的；广泛的，与 broadcast 同源

senses.title: A programme sent out by radio
senses.definition: a programme sent out by radio or television
senses.definitionCN: 由电台或电视台发送的节目
senses.example: The evening broadcast lasts an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间广播节目时长一小时。
senses.why: The noun names the thing that has been scattered out to many listeners.
senses.whyCN: 名词指被撒向众多听众的那个东西。

senses.title: To send out a programme
senses.definition: to send out a programme by radio or television
senses.definitionCN: 通过电台或电视发送节目
senses.example: The station will broadcast the match at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 电台将在八点播送这场比赛。
senses.why: Seeds cast broadly reach many fields; signals reach many homes.
senses.whyCN: 种子撒得广能到许多田里，信号也能进许多人家。

senses.title: To spread news widely
senses.definition: to tell a piece of news to many people
senses.definitionCN: 把消息告诉很多人
senses.example: He broadcast the rumour to the whole class.
senses.exampleCN: 他把这个传闻传给了全班。
senses.why: The radio image of wide scattering was applied to gossip.
senses.whyCN: 广播「广撒」的形象被用到了流言上。

intro.en: Broadcast joined broad and cast, first for sowing seed, then for sending signals.
intro.cn: broadcast 由 broad 与 cast 合成，先指撒种，后指发送信号。

items.en: broadcast meant to scatter seed over a wide field.
items.cn: broadcast 指把种子撒在宽阔的田里。

items.en: The word extended to spreading news among people.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到在人群中散布消息。

items.en: Radio gave broadcast its modern sense of sending sound.
items.cn: 无线电让 broadcast 有了发送声音的现代义。

items.en: Television widened it from sound to pictures.
items.cn: 电视把它从声音扩展到画面。

items.en: broadcast covers radio, television and online streaming.
items.cn: 如今 broadcast 涵盖电台、电视与网络直播。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the broad- opening; the near-meaning group gives other words for sending out.
note.cn: 形近组都以 broad- 开头；近义组是表示发送、传送的词。

entries.definition: wide from side to side

to send out signals

normalIntro.en: Broadcast is broad plus cast: cast the sound widely.

normal.en: A live broadcast goes out as it happens.
normal.cn: live broadcast 指现场直播。

normal.en: One person is a broadcaster.

normal.en: The past tense stays broadcast.

normal.en: The -ing form is broadcasting.
normal.cn: 现在分词是 broadcasting。

abstract.cn: 想象塔上闪着的红灯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red light on a transmission tower at night.

branches.cn: 现场直播

branches.cn: 晚间节目

intro.en: Broadcast is a compound that takes -er and -ing to name people and the industry.
intro.cn: broadcast 是合成词，加 -er 与 -ing 可表示人和行业。

definition_en: a line of bushes forming a fence, to surround with such bushes, or to avoid giving a direct answer
core_image: 花园边上修剪整齐的一排灌木，像一道绿色的墙
scene: 花园四周有一圈高高的树篱。 A tall hedge surrounds the garden.

pos.zh: 闪烁其词；避免正面回答

senses.title: A line of bushes
senses.definition: a row of bushes planted as a fence
senses.definitionCN: 种成一排、起围栏作用的灌木
senses.example: A tall hedge surrounds the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 花园四周有一圈高高的树篱。
senses.why: This is the living fence you can see.
senses.whyCN: 这是看得见的活篱笆。

senses.title: Surround with bushes
senses.definition: to plant or trim bushes around an area
senses.definitionCN: 在四周种植或修剪灌木以围住某地
senses.example: They hedged the field last spring.

senses.why: The noun turns into the act of building it.

senses.title: Avoid a direct answer

senses.definitionCN: 避免明确回答，或为防范风险留后路
senses.example: The manager hedged when asked about the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 被问及延误时，经理闪烁其词。
senses.why: A hedge hides what is behind it.

intro.en: Hedge comes from Old English hecg, a fence of bushes.
intro.cn: hedge 来自古英语 hecg，指灌木做成的篱笆。

items.en: Hecg named a boundary of bushes.

items.en: Related words named a fence or enclosure.

items.en: Hegge kept the sense of a field border.

items.en: To hedge became to protect against loss.
items.cn: to hedge 引申为防范损失。

items.en: Hedging words soften a direct answer.

note.en: Hedge is compared with look-alike words and with words for a barrier.

entries.definition: the outer limit of something

a small sign worn on clothes
a barrier around an area
a woody plant smaller than a tree
something that blocks the way

normalIntro.en: Hedge is a fence that grew, and then a way of hiding behind words.

normal.en: The hedge needs trimming.

normal.en: They hedged the garden with roses.

normal.en: He hedged when asked for a date.

normal.en: She hedged her bets and applied twice.

abstract.en: A hedge is a wall that keeps growing.

abstract.en: Words can be hedges too.
abstract.cn: 话语也能当作树篱。

abstract.en: To hedge is to leave a door open behind you.
abstract.cn: 留后路，就是在身后留一扇门。

examples.en: A tall hedge surrounds the garden.

examples.en: They hedged the field last spring.

examples.en: The manager hedged when asked about the delay.

senses.title: Group of ships

senses.title: Fast

normal.en: The years fleet past.
normal.cn: 岁月飞逝。

normal.en: A fleeting glance is very short.
normal.cn: fleeting 的一瞥极为短暂。

abstract.en: Many separate ships become one force when they sail together.
abstract.cn: 许多单独的船一起航行时成为一股力量。

abstract.en: Speed is measured best against something still.
abstract.cn: 速度最好相对于静止之物来衡量。

abstract.en: What passes quickly is remembered in outlines.
abstract.cn: 快速消逝之物只留下轮廓被记住。

examples.en: The fishing fleet left the harbour at dawn.
examples.cn: 渔船队清晨驶出港口。

examples.en: The company runs a fleet of buses.
examples.cn: 这家公司运营一支公交车队。

examples.en: The fleet deer outran the dogs.
examples.cn: 迅捷的鹿跑得比狗快。

dict_mnemonic.text: fleet 由古英语 fleot（船）与古诺尔斯语 fljotr（迅捷）汇合，兼有「船队」与「快速」两义。

root: 古英语 fleot（船、漂浮物）与古诺尔斯语 fljotr（迅捷）汇合，核心义「成群的船」与「快」。

sensesIntro.en: Fleet means a group of ships, vehicles, or aircraft, or fast in movement.
sensesIntro.cn: fleet 意为船队、车队、机群，或移动迅速。

core.en: A group moving together, or moving fast.
core.cn: 一起移动的群体，或移动得很快。

branches.en: Ships sailing as one body.
branches.cn: 作为一个整体航行的船。

branches.en: Vehicles or aircraft in one group.
branches.cn: 同一群体中的车辆或飞机。

branches.en: A literary word for swift.
branches.cn: 文学语体中表示迅捷。

branches.en: Time passing like a fast ship.
branches.cn: 时间像快船一样流逝。

branches.en: The group and the speed share one spelling.
branches.cn: 群体与速度共用一个拼写。

intro.en: Fleet builds a compact family around ships and swiftness.
intro.cn: fleet 围绕船只与迅捷构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Fleet has no Latin ancestor; Latin classis, a fleet, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: fleet 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 classis（舰队）只是语义对应词。

items.exampleCN: 我们看见一个一闪而过的影子。

items.example: The deer is known for fleetness.

definition_zh: 戒除；节制；禁欲；（宗教）斋戒；（政治）弃权
definition_en: the practice of deliberately not doing or consuming something, especially something pleasurable or harmful
core_image: 一只手伸到酒杯前，又稳稳地收回来
scene: 餐桌上摆着一瓶刚开的红酒，主人却把杯子推开了。 After years of trouble, he chose complete abstinence from alcohol.
sceneCN: 这里 abstinence 是「戒酒」（第 2 个义项：不再饮酒的自我约束）；句意为在多年麻烦之后，他选择了彻底戒酒。

pos.zh: 名词：戒除；节制；禁欲；斋戒；弃权

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ent 构成，义为「有节制的；戒除的」
同出拉丁语 abstinere 的动词，义为「戒除；弃权」
由本词加 -ious 构成的罕见形容词，义为「惯于节制的」

senses.title: Deliberately not doing something pleasurable
senses.definition: the practice of choosing not to do or take something that one enjoys, usually for a moral or personal reason
senses.definitionCN: 出于道德或个人理由，主动选择不做或不取用自己喜欢的事物
senses.example: His doctor recommended a short abstinence from rich food.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议他短期戒食油腻食物。
senses.why: Latin abstinere is 'to hold away from'; the picture is a hand held back just before it grasps.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abstinere 意为「握住、使之远离」，画面是一只手在抓住之前被稳稳地收住。

senses.title: Giving up alcohol
senses.definition: the decision to drink no alcohol at all, often as a promise to oneself or to a group
senses.definitionCN: 完全不饮酒的决定，常是对自己或对某个团体作出的承诺
senses.example: He signed a pledge of total abstinence at the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 他在诊所签下了完全戒酒的承诺。
senses.why: The held-back hand is most often pictured at a glass, so this is the word's best-known branch.
senses.whyCN: 收住的手最常出现在酒杯前，因此这是这个词最广为人知的一支。

senses.title: Sexual continence
senses.definition: the practice of not having sex, usually for religious, moral or personal reasons
senses.definitionCN: 出于宗教、道德或个人原因而不发生性行为
senses.example: The order required abstinence from all members.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会要求全体成员禁欲。
senses.why: The same holding back applies to desire itself: the body is kept from what it wants.
senses.whyCN: 同一种收住被用到欲望本身：身体被拦住，不去得到它想要的东西。

senses.title: A period of staying off an addiction
senses.definition: a period, often in treatment, during which a person stays completely away from a drug or habit
senses.definitionCN: 治疗过程中完全远离某种药物或习惯的一段时间
senses.example: The programme begins with a month of abstinence.
senses.exampleCN: 该疗程从一个月戒断期开始。
senses.why: A period of holding away becomes a measurable stage on the road to recovery.
senses.whyCN: 一段「持续收住」的时间，就成了康复道路上可衡量的阶段。

senses.title: Refusing to vote
senses.definition: the act of choosing not to vote on a question, either by leaving the ballot blank or by formally abstaining
senses.definitionCN: 选择不对某个问题投票，或留白，或正式声明弃权
senses.example: Three members chose abstinence rather than a no vote.
senses.exampleCN: 三名成员选择弃权而不是投反对票。
senses.why: In voting, the hand is held back from the ballot box: not a no, just no mark at all.
senses.whyCN: 在投票中，手被拦在票箱之外：不是反对，只是完全不留痕迹。

senses.title: Religious fasting and self-denial
senses.definition: in religious use, the practice of going without food, meat or other comforts on set days
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语境中在指定日子不吃食物、肉类或其他享受的做法
senses.example: Friday abstinence from meat is traditional in many churches.
senses.exampleCN: 许多教会都有周五戒食肉类的传统。
senses.why: Food is the most ancient thing a hand can be held back from, so fasting is the oldest branch of the word.
senses.whyCN: 食物是手最古老可以收住的对象，因此斋戒是这个词语义最古老的一支。

senses.title: Medical restriction of food or drink
senses.definition: a medical instruction that a patient must not eat or drink anything for a set time, especially before surgery
senses.definitionCN: 医嘱要求病人在一段时间内不得进食饮水，尤指手术之前
senses.example: The nurse checked that the patient had kept the required abstinence.
senses.exampleCN: 护士核对了病人是否遵守规定的禁食。
senses.why: Here the hand is held back not by desire but by rule, and the reason is safety.
senses.whyCN: 这里收住手不是出于欲望，而是出于规定，理由是安全。

senses.title: A general policy of restraint
senses.definition: a stated rule or habit of limiting indulgence in general, not limited to one substance or act
senses.definitionCN: 一种公开的规则或习惯，泛指对各种放纵加以限制，不限某一种物质或行为
senses.example: The community valued abstinence in dress, speech and diet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体在衣着、言谈和饮食上都推崇节制。
senses.why: The picture widens: what is held back is not one cup but every form of indulgence at once.
senses.whyCN: 画面变宽了：被拦住的不是一只酒杯，而是同时对所有形式的放纵。

intro.en: Abstinence comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold oneself away, and every sense is that gesture at a different scale.
intro.cn: abstinence 来自拉丁语中表示「使自己保持远离」的动词，每个义项都是这一姿态的不同尺度。

items.en: The verb tenere meant 'to hold, keep, grasp'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 tenere 意为「握住、保持、抓牢」；其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Abs- plus tenere formed abstinere, 'to hold back from, refrain from', literally to keep oneself away.
items.cn: abs- 加 tenere 构成 abstinere，意为「收住、远离、戒除」，字面就是使自己保持在外。

items.en: The abstract noun abstinentia named the habit or virtue of holding back, especially from food and drink.
items.cn: 抽象名词 abstinentia 指「收住」的习惯或美德，尤指在饮食方面的节制。

items.en: Old French carried the noun into English with the religious sense already well established.
items.cn: 古法语把这一名词带入英语，宗教义当时已相当稳固。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English in the thirteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这一名词在十三世纪见于英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Medical and parliamentary uses were added later, but all of them still describe a hand held back.
items.cn: 医学义与议会义是后来加上的，但它们都仍在描述一只被收住的手。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the tenere family; the near-meaning group gathers words for restraint, self-denial and the act of staying away.
note.cn: 形近组收 tenere 词族的词；近义组收表示节制、苦修与远离的词语。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hold back from something or to refuse to vote; the direct source of abstinence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「戒除、弃权」，是 abstinence 的直接来源，同出拉丁语 abstinere。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person who habitually holds back from indulgence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有节制的、戒除的」，由本词加 -ent 构成。

entries.definition: To hold something inside limits; it shares the Latin holding verb tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳、控制」，共用拉丁语「握持」动词 tenere，词根同源。

entries.definition: To keep something and not let it go; another English word built on tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「保留、留住」，同样建立在 tenere 之上，词根同源。

entries.definition: Ridiculous; it shares the abs- opening but comes from surdus, deaf.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒谬的」，只是同样以 abs- 开头，词根为 surdus「聋的」，词源不同。

entries.definition: Keeping amounts within reasonable limits; it allows some, while abstinence allows none.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适度、节制」，允许少量，而 abstinence 是完全不许。

entries.definition: Deliberately giving up things one wants, often as a discipline or a religious exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自我克制、苦修」，有意放弃想要的东西，多作修炼或宗教功课。

entries.definition: Going without food for a period, usually for religious or health reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「禁食」，在一段时间内不吃东西，多出于宗教或健康原因。

entries.definition: The virtue of restraining one's desires, especially in drinking; older and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节制、禁酒」，尤指饮酒有度，语气较古雅正式。

entries.definition: The act of allowing oneself something one enjoys; the direct opposite of holding back.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「放纵、沉溺」，指允许自己享受所好之物，正与收住相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real tenere root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 tenere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Tenere is to hold: abstinence is holding yourself away from a thing, not losing it.
normal.cn: tenere 是「握住」：abstinence 是把自己握在远离某物的一侧，而不是失去它。

normal.en: The same root appears in contain and retain, both of which are about keeping hold.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 contain 与 retain，两者都与握持有关。

normal.en: Abstinence from alcohol is the pledge made at the start of many recovery programmes.
normal.cn: abstinence from alcohol 是许多康复疗程开始时作出的承诺。

normal.en: In a vote, abstention is the same held-back hand, just without leaving a mark.
normal.cn: 在投票中，弃权是同一只收住的手，只是不留任何痕迹。

normal.en: Religious abstinence from meat is tied to fixed days in the church calendar.
normal.cn: 宗教上的戒食肉类与教会历法中的固定日子相绑定。

abstract.en: Picture a glass lifted halfway and then set down again while it is still full.
abstract.cn: 想象一只酒杯被举到一半，又原样放回桌面，杯里仍是满的。

abstract.en: The same gesture works for sweets, for speech, for a ballot and for desire itself.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作也适用于甜食、言语、选票以及欲望本身。

abstract.en: Abstinence is not absence: the thing is still there, and the choice is renewed each time.
abstract.cn: abstinence 不是「没有」：东西仍在眼前，只是每次都要重新作出选择。

examples.en: The clinic asks patients to keep strict abstinence during treatment.
examples.cn: 诊所要求病人在治疗期间严格戒断。

examples.en: His abstinence from sweets lasted exactly one week.
examples.cn: 他戒甜食只坚持了整整一周。

examples.en: Two councillors declared their abstinence on the final motion.
examples.cn: 两名议员在最终动议上宣布弃权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布斯提能斯」——手伸到杯前又停住，能忍住不喝：节制、戒除

root: 拉丁语 abstinentia 由 abstinere「收住、远离、戒除」加抽象名词后缀构成，abstinere 则是 abs-「离开」+ tenere「握持」；tenere 更早来源不确定。核心是「把自己握在远离某物的一侧」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same pause: the hand is held back from food, alcohol, sex, a drug, a ballot, meat, a meal before surgery, or indulgence in general.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一个停顿：手被收住，不去碰食物、酒、性、毒品、选票、肉类、术前饮食，或一切放纵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches toward a filled glass and is pulled back before it touches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向斟满的杯子，在触到之前又收了回来。

branches.en: THE GENERAL RULE: any pleasure, and any indulgence at all, can be the thing the hand stays away from.
branches.cn: 通则线：任何享受、任何放纵，都可以成为手所远离的对象。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: alcohol and drugs are met with a held-back hand over a whole period of time.
branches.cn: 物质线：面对酒与毒品，收住的手要持续整段时间。

branches.en: THE BODY: desire itself is what the hand refuses, and the body is kept from acting.
branches.cn: 身体线：手拒绝的是欲望本身，身体因此不作出行动。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE RITE: fasting and medical bans both turn the gesture into a prescribed practice.
branches.cn: 规矩与礼俗线：斋戒与医嘱禁食都把这一姿态变成规定的做法。

branches.en: THE BALLOT: in voting, the hand stops short of the box and leaves no mark.
branches.cn: 选票线：在投票时手停在票箱之外，不留任何痕迹。

intro.en: Abstinence is a Latin prefix plus a Latin holding verb, lengthened into a noun; English adds two small suffixes.
intro.cn: abstinence 由拉丁语前缀加「握持」动词构成，并拉长为名词；英语又加了两个小后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere, abstinere and abstinentia are all recorded, so only the older root of tenere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere、abstinere 与 abstinentia 均有记录，只有 tenere 更早的词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks distance from the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记与对象的距离。

items.example: The verb is the holding root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「握持」词根。

items.example: The compound verb names the act of keeping away.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词指保持远离的动作。

items.example: The noun turned the act into a virtue.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把动作变成了美德。
它与 abstinentia 一起构成 abstinence。

items.meaning: to refrain, to decline to vote
items.example: Members may abstain on the motion.
items.exampleCN: 成员可以对该动议弃权。

items.example: The same holding verb appears with a different prefix.
items.exampleCN: 同一个「握持」动词配上不同的前缀。

items.example: The company retained its best engineers.
items.exampleCN: 公司留住了最好的工程师。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ent 构成，义为「有节制的；戒除的」
由同一拉丁词根构成，义为「戒除；弃权」

definition_en: to become involved in a situation in order to change it, or to come between two things
core_image: 两个人正吵着，一只手从中间伸进来把他们隔开
scene: 楼下两人越吵越凶，邻居从门里出来站在他们中间劝架。 The teacher intervened before the quarrel turned into a fight.
sceneCN: 这里 intervene 是「干预」（第 1 个义项：介入以改变局面），句意为老师赶在争吵变成打架之前介入了。画面里的物件：楼梯口、半开的门、伸出的手臂。

pos.zh: 动词：干预；介入；插入；发生在其间

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -tion 构成，义为「干预；介入」
由现在分词构成，义为「介于其间的」
同一词根 venire 构成，义为「召集」
同一词根 venire 构成，义为「阻止」

senses.title: Step into a quarrel
senses.definition: to involve oneself in a dispute or bad situation in order to alter the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 为改变结果而置身于争执或坏局面之中
senses.example: A neighbour intervened and pulled the two men apart.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居介入，把两个人拉开。
senses.why: Latin venire means to come; to intervene is to come in between other people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 venire 意为「来」，intervene 就是「走到别人中间来」。

senses.title: Come in as a third force
senses.definition: to act from outside so as to stop or change what two others are doing
senses.definitionCN: 从外部行动以阻止或改变另外两方所做的事
senses.example: The central bank intervened to calm the currency market.
senses.exampleCN: 央行出面干预以稳定货币市场。
senses.why: Institutions borrow the quarrel sense for markets and states.
senses.whyCN: 机构把劝架义借到市场与国家事务上。

senses.title: Come between in time
senses.definition: to occur between two points in time so as to separate them
senses.definitionCN: 发生在两个时点之间，把它们隔开
senses.example: Two wars intervened before the treaty was signed.
senses.exampleCN: 条约签订之前隔着两场战争。
senses.why: The literal coming-between survives here with no one acting at all.
senses.whyCN: 这里保留字面上的「来到中间」，却没有任何人动手。

senses.title: Happen in between
senses.definition: to lie or happen between two other things in space or in a sequence
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上或次序上位于另外两事物之间
senses.example: A narrow lane intervenes between the two gardens.
senses.exampleCN: 两座花园之间夹着一条窄巷。
senses.why: Space and sequence keep the oldest, most neutral use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 空间与次序保留了这个词最古老、最中性的用法。

intro.en: Intervene joins Latin inter- "between" with venire "to come".
intro.cn: intervene 把拉丁语 inter-「之间」与 venire「来」结合在一起。

items.en: Venire meant to come or to approach.
items.cn: venire 意为来到或走近。

items.en: Intervenire meant to come in between or to interrupt.
items.cn: intervenire 意为走到中间来或插进来。

items.en: French intervenir kept the legal sense of a third party stepping in.
items.cn: 法语 intervenir 保留了第三方出面的法律义。

items.en: English law used intervene for a party joining a suit.
items.cn: 英国法律用 intervene 指当事人加入诉讼。

items.en: Politics and medicine widened it to any outside action.
items.cn: 政治与医学又把它扩展到任何外部行动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vene root of coming; the near-meaning group holds other words for stepping in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -vene「来」词根；近义组收其他表示「出面」的词。

entries.definition: The act of stepping in from outside.
To call people together to meet.
To come before and stop something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「阻止」，字面是「先来」.

entries.definition: To get involved where one is not wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「干涉」，常含不受欢迎之意。

entries.definition: To help two sides reach agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「调解」，居中促成和解。

entries.definition: To take action to help or stop something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语义为「出面」，偏口语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the coming verb venire, which is hidden in many English words.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用「来」这个动词 venire，它藏在许多英语词里。

normal.en: inter- between plus venire come equals coming between.
normal.cn: inter-「之间」加 venire「来」等于「来到中间」。

normal.en: Convene and prevent carry the same coming root.
normal.cn: convene 与 prevent 带着同一个「来」的词根。

normal.en: To intervene in a quarrel is to arrive where you were not invited.
normal.cn: intervene in a quarrel 是来到一个没人请你的地方。

normal.en: The bank intervened, the referee intervened: both step in.
normal.cn: 银行介入、裁判介入，都是 step in。

normal.en: Two years intervened before they met again.
normal.cn: 他们再见面之前隔了两年。

abstract.en: Intervention is a hand laid on someone else's story.
abstract.cn: 干预是一只手搭在别人的故事上。

abstract.en: The intervener chooses sides by merely arriving.
abstract.cn: 介入者只要到场，就已经选了边。

abstract.en: Some years merely pass; others intervene.
abstract.cn: 有些年份只是过去，有些则横在中间。

examples.en: The referee intervened when the players began pushing.
examples.cn: 球员开始推搡时裁判介入了。

examples.en: Several quiet years intervened before the letters came.
examples.cn: 来信之前隔了好几个平静的年头。

examples.en: Doctors intervened in time to save his sight.
examples.cn: 医生及时干预，保住了他的视力。

dict_mnemonic.text: inter（之间）+ ven（来）+ e——走到中间来

root: 拉丁语 venire「来」→ intervenire「来到中间」→ 古法语 intervenir → 英语 intervene。同族有 intervention、convene、prevent。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: step into a quarrel, act as an outside force, come between in time, and lie in between.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：介入争执、作为第三方出面、在时间上隔在中间，以及空间上夹在中间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushed in between two people who are shouting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手臂伸进两个正在大声争吵的人之间。

branches.en: THE NEIGHBOUR: someone arrives and pulls them apart.
branches.cn: 邻居这条线：有人来到中间把人拉开。

branches.en: THE BANK: an institution acts from outside.
branches.cn: 银行这条线：机构从外部动手。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: empty years sit between two dates.
branches.cn: 日历这条线：两个日期之间隔着几年。

branches.en: THE LANE: a narrow path squeezed between gardens.
branches.cn: 小巷这条线：被两座花园夹住的路。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses need an outsider to arrive.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都需要一个外来者到场。

intro.en: Intervene is inter- "between" plus the Latin verb venire "to come".
intro.cn: intervene 是 inter-「之间」加拉丁动词 venire「来」。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire, intervenire and the participle interventus are all recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 venire、intervenire 与分词 interventus 均有记载。

items.example: It forms prevent, to come before.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 prevent，意为先来一步。

core_image: 停在路边的抛锚汽车
scene: 汽车在高速路边抛锚。 The car had a breakdown on the highway.
sceneCN: 这里 breakdown 是「故障」（第 1 个义项：机器或系统停止运转）；句意是汽车在高速路边抛锚。

pos.zh: 名词：故障；崩溃；分类细目

senses.title: A machine failure
senses.definition: a time when a machine stops working
senses.definitionCN: 机器停止运转的情况
senses.example: The car had a breakdown on the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在高速路边抛锚。
senses.why: The verb break down turned into one noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词短语 break down 合成了一个名词。

senses.title: A collapse of health or talks
senses.definition: a sudden failure of health or of an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 健康或协议的突然崩溃
senses.example: He suffered a breakdown from overwork.
senses.exampleCN: 他因过度劳累而精神崩溃。
senses.why: A stopped machine pictured a stopped mind or plan.
senses.whyCN: 停下的机器被用来比喻停摆的心智或计划。

senses.title: A list of separate parts
senses.definition: a list that separates something into its parts
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物拆成各个部分的清单
senses.example: She asked for a breakdown of the costs.
senses.exampleCN: 她要求提供费用明细。
senses.why: Breaking a whole into parts produced this sense.
senses.whyCN: 把整体拆成部分，就产生了这个义项。

intro.en: Breakdown joined break and down in English to name a collapse.
intro.cn: breakdown 由 break 与 down 在英语中组合，表示垮掉。

items.en: break down named a fall into pieces.

items.en: breakdown named a collapse of health.
items.cn: breakdown 指健康的垮掉。

items.en: breakdown named a machine failure.
items.cn: breakdown 指机器故障。

items.en: breakdown named a list of parts.

items.en: breakdown covers machines, health and costs.

abstract.cn: 想象冒烟的机器。

abstract.en: See a bill split into small lines.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a car stopped at the roadside with smoke.
core.cn: 核心意象：冒着烟停在路边的汽车。

branches.cn: 发动机故障

branches.en: breakdown cover

branches.cn: 精神崩溃

branches.cn: 费用明细

intro.cn: breakdown 由 break 与 down 及其他小品词组合。

latinIntro.cn: 词基来自英语，下面的拉丁词只在意思上相关。

definition_zh: 垫子；小地毯；门口地垫；体操垫；缠结的一团
definition_en: a flat piece of material laid on a surface for protection or comfort, a small rug at a door, a thick padded sheet used in sport, or a thick tangled mass
core_image: 一块粗糙的草席铺在地上，鞋底的泥都落在它上面
scene: 雨刚停，杂货铺门口的水泥地上摊着一块深色垫子，进门的人都在上面蹭两下鞋底。 A faded mat lay by the shop door and caught the mud from every boot.
sceneCN: 这里 mat 是「门口地垫；小地毯」（第 2 个义项：铺在门口、供人蹭鞋的小块织物）；句意为门边摊着一块褪色的垫子，接住每双靴子带进来的泥。图中可辨识物件：湿水泥地、褪色垫子、进门的人。

pos.zh: 垫子；小地毯；体操垫；缠结的一团

derivatives.zh: 由 mat 加表示「材料、结果」的后缀 -ing 构成，义为「编垫的材料；垫子总称」
由 mat 加 -ed 构成，义为「缠结成团的；压成一片的」
由 door 与 mat 复合而成，义为「门垫」，也指任人欺负的人

senses.title: A flat pad laid on a surface
senses.definition: a flat piece of material placed on a table, floor or other surface to protect it or to set things on
senses.definitionCN: 铺在桌面、地面或其他表面，用来保护表面或放置物品的平整物件
senses.example: A woven mat kept the hot pot from marking the table.
senses.exampleCN: 一只编织垫隔在热锅与桌面之间，免得留下痕迹。
senses.why: Late Latin matta named a coarse woven cloth, so the object began as something spread flat and porous rather than as a solid slab.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 matta 指粗糙的编织布，所以这件东西起初是一块摊平而透气的织物，而不是实心的板。

senses.title: A small rug at a door
senses.definition: a small piece of material placed at a door or beside a bed for people to wipe their feet or stand on
senses.definitionCN: 铺在门口或床边，供人蹭脚或站立的小块织物
senses.example: Mud from the lane was still wet on the door mat.
senses.exampleCN: 巷子里的泥在门口地垫上还湿着。
senses.why: Once a woven cloth lies where feet pass, it takes on the job of catching dirt, and the word moves from the cloth to the place it guards.
senses.whyCN: 当一块编织布铺在人脚经过的地方，它便担起了接住污垢的职责，词义也从布本身转到它所守护的那个位置。

senses.title: A thick padded mat for sport
senses.definition: a thick padded mat spread on a floor for gymnastics, wrestling or other training
senses.definitionCN: 铺在地上、供体操、摔跤或其他训练使用的厚实衬垫
senses.example: The coach spread a mat beneath the beam before the routine.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在平衡木下铺好垫子，才让队员开始动作。
senses.why: The same flat spread appears again in the gym, but here it must absorb a falling body, so thickness replaces the thin woven surface.
senses.whyCN: 同一块摊平的东西在体育馆里再次出现，只是这次要接住跌倒的身体，于是厚度取代了薄薄的编织面。

senses.title: A thick tangled mass
senses.definition: a thick mass of hair, grass or other material that has become tangled together
senses.definitionCN: 头发、草或其他材料缠结在一起形成的一团厚实物
senses.example: The rain had pressed the grass into a flat mat.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水把草压成了一片贴地的草毡。
senses.why: A mat is made of many strands pressed flat into one layer, so any tangle of strands squeezed into a layer can borrow the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 垫子本由许多细条压平、摊成一层，于是任何被挤成一层的细条团都能借用同一个画面。

intro.en: Mat is a plain word for a coarse woven spread; it reached English through Germanic forms from Late Latin matta, whose deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: mat 是个朴素的词，指粗糙的编织铺物；它经日耳曼语形式从晚期拉丁语 matta 进入英语，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Matta named a coarse cloth or mat woven from rushes, the sort spread on a floor or used to wrap goods.
items.cn: matta 指用灯心草编成的粗布或席子，正是铺在地上或用来包东西的那一种。

items.en: The source of matta is uncertain; some accounts suggest a North African or Punic origin, but no Latin cognate settles the question.
items.cn: matta 的来源不确定；有些说法推测它出自北非或布匿语，但没有任何拉丁同族词能定论。

items.en: Old English matte named a mat or a bed of rushes, and it kept the plain sense of something spread flat.
items.cn: 古英语 matte 指席子或草铺，保留了「摊平铺开」这一朴素意思。

items.en: Middle English dropped the final vowel and wrote mat, while matting named both the material and the work of weaving it.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉词尾元音，写作 mat；matting 则兼指材料与编织这门活。

items.en: Modern English keeps the floor sense and extends it to gym padding, table mats and any thick tangled mass.
items.cn: 现代英语保留铺地之义，并把它扩展到体操垫、餐桌垫，以及任何缠结成一团的厚实物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and one close spelling; the near group gathers other flat things laid down for comfort or protection.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收其他为舒适或保护而铺开的扁平物件。

entries.definition: Material woven into mats, or mats taken together.
entries.definitionCN: 编成垫子的材料，或垫子的总称；由 mat 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Pressed or tangled into a thick mass.
entries.definitionCN: 被压成或缠成一团的；由 mat 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: A mat placed at a door, or a person who accepts being treated badly.
entries.definitionCN: 放在门口的垫子；也指任人欺负的人；由 door 与 mat 复合而成。

entries.definition: Having a dull, non-shiny surface; the spelling is close but the word comes from another source.
entries.definitionCN: 表面无光泽的；只是拼写相近，词源不同，与 mat 无关。

entries.definition: A small carpet for part of a floor.
entries.definitionCN: 铺在地面一部分的小地毯。

entries.definition: A thick piece of soft material used for protection or comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 起保护或衬垫作用的厚软物。

entries.definition: A bag of soft material that supports the body or a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 支撑身体或表面的软垫。

entries.definition: A woven covering for a whole floor.
entries.definitionCN: 铺满整片地面的编织覆盖物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a flat woven spread at heart, and its family keeps returning to layers laid down, pressed together and finally tangled.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词骨子里就是一块摊平的编织铺物，它的同族词反复回到铺下的一层、压在一起的一层，最后缠成一团。

normal.en: Late Latin matta was a coarse cloth of rushes, so a mat was never a solid object but a flat woven sheet.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁语 matta 是灯心草编的粗布，所以垫子从来不是实心物件，而是一块摊平的编织片。

normal.en: Old English matte kept that sense and passed it on as the modern word mat.
normal.cn: 古英语 matte 保留了这层意思，后来传成现代词 mat。

normal.en: Matting adds -ing and names the material or the whole set of mats, not one mat.
normal.cn: matting 加 -ing，指材料或垫子的总称，而不是某一块垫子。

normal.en: Matted adds -ed and describes strands that have been pressed into one layer, like wet hair.
normal.cn: matted 加 -ed，形容细条被压成一层，就像湿透的头发。

normal.en: Doormat joins door and mat; the figurative sense comes from people wiping their feet on someone.
normal.cn: doormat 由 door 与 mat 拼成；比喻义来自人们把脚在某人身上蹭干净。

abstract.en: A mat is a boundary: it takes the dirt so the floor behind it stays clean.
abstract.cn: 垫子是一道边界：它接下污垢，让背后的地面保持干净。

abstract.en: The same flat layer can protect a table, a wrestler or a field of grass, because the shape is simple enough to travel.
abstract.cn: 同一层扁平之物既能护住桌面、摔跤手，也能盖住一片草，因为形状足够简单，可以被搬到各处。

abstract.en: What is spread flat can later be pressed flat, and the word follows the strands all the way into a tangle.
abstract.cn: 摊平的东西后来会被压平，这个词就跟着那些细条一路走进缠结之中。

examples.en: She rolled up her yoga mat and left the studio.
examples.cn: 她卷起瑜伽垫，离开了练习室。

examples.en: The rain had pressed the grass into a flat mat.
examples.cn: 雨水把草压成了一片贴地的草毡。

examples.en: Mud from the lane was still wet on the door mat.
examples.cn: 巷子里的泥在门口地垫上还湿着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马特」——马特进门之前先在垫子上蹭两下鞋；记住 mat 是垫子，也是门口那块蹭鞋的小毯。

root: 晚期拉丁语 matta（灯心草编的粗席）经日耳曼语形式进入古英语作 matte，再演变为 mat；matta 更早的来源一般认为可能出自北非或布匿语，但存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a flat woven layer spread on a surface; the senses then divide into the protective pad, the small rug at a door, the thick gym padding and the tangled mass.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是铺在表面上的一层扁平编织物；义项由此分成护面的垫子、门口的小毯、体育馆里的厚垫，以及缠结成的一团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coarse woven square laid on the ground, taking the mud from every passing boot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块粗糙的编织方席铺在地上，接下每双经过的靴子带来的泥。

branches.en: a hot pot set down on a woven square
branches.cn: 热锅落在编织方垫上

branches.en: wet boots stopping at a shop door
branches.cn: 湿靴子在店门口停住

branches.en: a body landing on thick padding under a beam
branches.cn: 身体落在平衡木下的厚垫上

branches.en: wet grass pressed flat after a night of rain
branches.cn: 一夜雨后贴地压平的湿草

branches.en: thin under a plate, thick under a falling body
branches.cn: 薄的在盘下，厚的在跌落的身体下

intro.en: The word is carried by a Late Latin noun for coarse cloth, its Old English descendant, the English noun and three English endings that name material, state and a compound.
intro.cn: 这个词由晚期拉丁语里表示粗布的名词、它的古英语后代、英语名词本身，以及三个分别表示材料、状态与复合的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin matta is the recorded form behind the family; its deeper source is uncertain, so only that one Latin form is claimed.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 matta 是这个词族有记录的形式；它更早的来源不确定，因此只列出这一个拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 无害的；无恶意的；未受损伤的
definition_en: not able or likely to cause harm
core_image: 一条小蛇安静地盘在草丛里
scene: 这种蛇是无害的。 This snake is harmless.
sceneCN: 这里 harmless 是「无害的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这种蛇是无害的。

senses.title: Not dangerous
senses.definition: not able to hurt a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 不能伤害人或动物的
senses.example: This snake is harmless.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛇是无害的。
senses.why: This is the physical safety sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体安全层面的义项。

senses.title: Without bad intent
senses.definition: not meant to hurt or offend anyone
senses.definitionCN: 并非有意伤害或冒犯他人
senses.example: It was harmless fun.
senses.exampleCN: 那只是无伤大雅的玩笑。
senses.why: No harm in the body means no harm in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 身体无伤，心里也就没有恶意。

senses.title: Not damaged
senses.definition: not harmed or damaged after some event
senses.definitionCN: 经历某事之后未受伤损的
senses.example: The old church stood harmless after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后，老教堂安然无恙。
senses.why: A rare sense that describes the thing that escaped.
senses.whyCN: 这是描述「逃过一劫」之物的少见义项。

intro.en: Harmless is harm plus the ending -less, meaning without.
intro.cn: harmless 是 harm 加后缀 -less，意为「没有……的」。

items.en: Hearm meant injury.
items.cn: hearm 意为伤害。

items.en: The ending -less meant without.
items.cn: 后缀 -less 意为没有。

items.en: Harmless described safe animals.
items.cn: harmless 描述安全的动物。

items.en: It also described innocent jokes.
items.cn: 它也描述无恶意的玩笑。

items.en: The word named what escaped damage.
items.cn: 这个词也指未受损的事物。

note.en: Harmless is compared with look-alike words and with words for safety and innocence.
note.cn: 把 harmless 与形近词以及表示安全和善意的词作比较。

entries.definition: causing harm
unable to act
without a home
not likely to cause harm
not guilty or not harmful
not likely to upset anyone

normalIntro.en: Harmless is a thing with no harm in it, and a word with no knife in it.
normalIntro.cn: harmless 是没有伤害的东西，也是没有藏刀的一句话。

normal.en: Most spiders are harmless.
normal.cn: 大多数蜘蛛无害。

normal.en: The joke was harmless.

normal.en: The medicine is harmless to children.
normal.cn: 这种药对儿童无害。

normal.en: The old house stood harmless.
normal.cn: 老房子安然无恙。

normal.en: It looked harmless enough.
